**Converges.** The series Σ 1/(n³+1) converges.

I ran the query on Wolfram|Alpha (`sum from n=1 to infinity of 1/(n^3+1) convergence`). The page showed the input interpreted as `SumConvergence` and a step-by-step hint beginning "use the p-series to …", but the result itself is an image and didn't come through as text, so I couldn't read Wolfram's verdict directly.

The conclusion comes from the standard comparison test: 1/(n³+1) ÷ 1/n³ = n³/(n³+1) → 1 as n → ∞. Since Σ 1/n³ is a p-series with p = 3 > 1 and converges, Σ 1/(n³+1) converges by the limit comparison test.
